plan.scientific_mechanism: Rapid arrivals from matured latency can transiently dilute case recognition and withdrawal efficiency, so more later-stage occupancy is required to trigger the same effective removal from the observed contagious pool when latent inflow is high.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's fixed-threshold assumption for clearance activation rather than add a wholly new compartment. Varying condition: the endogenous latent inflow pressure progression_rate*C_latent changes over time under the existing initial conditions, while the biological interpretation of C, I_late, and the no-new-infections protocol is held fixed. Parent contrast: for any given C and I_late, the parent maps those states to one unique clearance contribution because late_half_saturation is constant. Child contrast: the same C and I_late can produce a different dC_dt depending on whether C_latent is still large, because high inflow shifts the effective activation scale upward and weakens removal. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not only auxiliary trajectories, since dC_dt directly gains dependence on C_latent beyond the existing linear inflow term. The effect is admissible when the trajectory spans an early high-inflow regime and a later low-inflow regime; under those conditions a single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both weaker early and stronger late clearance activation at comparable C and I_late, because its one shared threshold fixes one response shape across the whole run. If latent inflow is always negligible, the refinement becomes practically unidentifiable and the parent is recovered.

response_change.parent_relation: The clearance term depends on C and I_late through a single late_half_saturation scale, so the reduction in dC_dt is governed by one fixed occupancy threshold and cannot change shape with the latent inflow level except through current state magnitudes.
response_change.child_relation: Make the burden-dependent clearance activation threshold itself depend on contemporaneous latent-to-contagious inflow pressure, so the effect of I_late on dC_dt is weaker during strong C_latent-driven arrivals and stronger once inflow subsides.
response_change.observable_effect: At matched I_late and similar C, early times with high C_latent show less negative dC_dt than later times with depleted C_latent; this delays or broadens the contagious peak relative to the parent's single-threshold response.

contract.activation_condition: Observable when progression_rate*C_latent is initially appreciable relative to clearance_rate*C and then declines over the observation window, so the same range of C and I_late is visited under both high- and low-inflow conditions.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within a single no-new-infections trajectory, the mechanism is visible because C_latent starts high and later depletes, extending the parent law from one fixed activation threshold to an inflow-conditioned threshold over time.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the inflow modulation strength to zero, so late_half_saturation becomes a constant again.
contract.scientific_mechanism: Rapid arrivals from matured latency can transiently dilute case recognition and withdrawal efficiency, so more later-stage occupancy is required to trigger the same effective removal from the observed contagious pool when latent inflow is high.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the clearance response surface now changes with latent inflow pressure, creating a state-dependent threshold that alters the shape of dC_dt over the same C and I_late range rather than merely rescaling removal uniformly.
contract.assumption_before: Burden-dependent clearance activation uses a time-independent, inflow-independent half-saturation threshold.
contract.assumption_after: The effective late-stage clearance activation threshold increases monotonically with contemporaneous latent inflow pressure and relaxes as inflow subsides.
contract.parent_reduction: Setting inflow_clearance_modulation to zero gives the exact parent fragment.
contract.observable_signature: Compared at similar C and I_late along the same trajectory, dC_dt is less negative when progression_rate*C_latent is high and becomes more negative after C_latent depletion, because the effective clearance activation threshold is temporarily elevated during strong inflow. The parent cannot produce this high-inflow versus low-inflow threshold shift since it maps C and I_late to one fixed clearance shape once parameters are chosen.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both weaker early and stronger late clearance activation at comparable C and I_late, because its one shared late_half_saturation imposes one response curve for the entire run. Retuning clearance_rate or late_half_saturation only rescales or shifts that single curve globally; it cannot create the child's inflow-conditioned interaction where the same C and I_late yield different clearance strength depending on C_latent.
